title: Christmas Around the World
strapline: One festival, celebrated a hundred different ways — from snowy Sweden to sunny Australia — and every family's traditions welcome here.
intent: Christmas is celebrated in many different ways across the world and across families, and exploring that variety helps children see that there is no single 'right' way — and that their own family's traditions belong here too.
Meeting real celebrations from families in the community grows respect for difference and pride when a child's own customs are shared and honoured.
Making decorations, cards and gifts from different traditions invites rich creative and fine-motor work — folding, cutting, threading, wrapping.
The festival is full of mathematics — patterns on decorations, counting the days of an advent calendar, sorting and matching, one gift for each friend.
Children build knowledge of the wider world and language to talk about it — celebrate, decorate, tradition, gift, feast, star, share.
Giving cards and gifts, sharing food and welcoming everyone's traditions builds generosity, belonging and community.
implementation: Ask families how they celebrate — or if they mark a different winter festival — and build the provision from what they share, keeping it accurate and never assuming everyone celebrates the same way.
Explore a few different Christmas traditions from around the world — foods, decorations, weather, customs — and compare them with wonder, not ranking.
Offer decoration-, card- and gift-making, a wrapping station, and a role-play celebration table children can set and share.
Model the comparing talk: 'In some places it's snowy at Christmas and in others it's hot and sunny — what's it like where your family celebrates?'
Bring in maths — repeating patterns on decorations, counting down an advent calendar, matching a card to each friend, sharing food fairly.
Keep it inclusive — celebrate the winter festivals different families mark, and make sure every child sees something of their own home reflected.
key_questions: What is Christmas like where your family celebrates — snowy or sunny?
What pattern have you made on your decoration? What comes next?
How many days until we open the last advent window?
Have we got a card for every friend?
Which winter festival does your family celebrate at home?

impact.text: Children learn there is no single 'right' way to celebrate and that their own family's traditions belong here.

Children match and share — one gift, one card for each friend.
Children give, share food and welcome everyone's traditions, building generosity and belonging.

enhancements: A wrapping station and a role-play celebration table children can set and share.
Families invited to share how they celebrate, or a different winter festival they mark.
Decorations from different traditions compared with wonder, not ranking.
An advent count-down that brings daily counting into the run-up.
A card-making corner with one card matched to each friend.

playing_exploring: Children explore the colour, making and giving of a festival celebrated many ways, bringing their own family traditions to it.
They make, wrap, decorate and set the celebration together.
active_learning: Children see their decorations, cards and gifts through, and take part in preparing the shared celebration.
creating_thinking: Children compare how different families and places celebrate and make sense of traditions like and unlike their own.
